thread.title: Velodyne halves price on self-driving sensor Zoox, Apple are said to be using

author: Cromwell Schubarth
title: Velodyne halves price on self-driving sensor Zoox, Apple are said to be using
text: – TechFlash Editor, Silicon Valley Business Journal Jan 2, 2018, 7:03am PST Updated Jan 2, 2018, 7:07am PST Velodyne LiDAR Inc. started the New Year by slashing the price of a widely used self-driving vehicle sensor it makes by half amid increased competition. The company said it has doubled its workforce with the opening of its new "mega-factory" in San Jose and is able to cut prices while making its products in the U.S. Demand has soared for the sensor whose price is being cut — the VLP-16, according to founder and CEO David Hall . "As a result, we increased capacity and now can pass along savings as cost reduction to our customers,” he said in the announcement of the price reduction on Monday. “We want to make 2018 a year of optimism for the autonomous vehicle, especially as the first waves of robocabs hit the road." The VLP-16 sensor is the most popular LiDAR system on the market. Menlo Park-based Zoox Inc. is using it on its robo-taxis and Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) reportedly has installed at least six on an experimental vehicle. Competition is fierce among producers of the laser sensors made by Velodyne. While it slashed the price on its low-end system to about $4,000, the cost of its high-end system is about $85,000. That's about seven times what San Francisco-based rival Ouster Inc. charges for a comparable sensor. Another rival, Sunnyvale-based Quanergy Systems Inc., already sells a system for $4,000 and has predicted that it will get that cost down below $100 in the next three to four years. Quanergy has raised about $150 million from investors who include Daimler AG, Automotive Plc and Samsung Electronics who valued the business at about $1.5 billion its most recent round in August 2016. Velodyne raised about $150 million from Ford Motor Co. (NYSE:F) and Baidu (NASDAQ:BIDU) that same month at a valuation of about $1 billion. Oster has raised about $30 million from venture investors who include Fontinalis Partners , Amity Ventures, Constellation Technology Ventures, Tao Capital Partners and Carthona Capital. It is valued at about $200 million, according to PitchBook Data .
